datasets_from_scratch_no_english_source.evidence: TUMLU is 'a comprehensive, multilingual, and natively developed language understanding benchmark.' Data collected from publicly available books and websites in each target language; majority are sample or official questions for university entrance exams of respective countries. No English source material used. The Turkish subset (TurkishMMLU) is also natively developed in Turkish.

datasets_translated_from_english.evidence: No datasets are translated from English. The paper explicitly critiques translation-based benchmarks: 'most of these either cover a limited set of high-resourced languages, or the multilingual examples are generated by translating original examples from Western-centric languages, thus failing to capture cultural nuances inherent in different languages.'

details.TUMLU: Questions drawn from national educational curricula and university entrance exams. Includes culturally specific subjects: Native Language & Literature (language-specific), national History, Geography (region-relevant). Different countries' exam traditions represented.
details.TUMLU-mini: Subset of TUMLU; inherits cultural grounding from source material.

all_annotators_native_speakers.evidence: Paper states: 'native speakers of each language manually verified the quality of a random sample from each subject.' CoT prompts were 'created manually by native speakers.' Authors include native speakers of multiple Turkic languages based at institutions across Azerbaijan, Turkey, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan.

annotator_workforce.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The paper lists author affiliations but does not report total number of annotators, annotator demographics, compensation, or ethics/IRB review. Azerbaijani subset described as 'developed by the community' (referring to a community of students and teachers). Kazakh questions 'developed by a community of students and teachers.' Acknowledgments mention Ukrainian Center for Educational Quality Assessment (Crimean Tatar materials), Google Gemini Academic Program (compute credits), and Azerbaijan Cultural Society of Northern California (financial support).

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: The benchmark is explicitly designed to counter English-centricity. The paper argues that 'most multilingual examples are generated by translating original examples from Western-centric languages, thus failing to capture cultural nuances.' TUMLU uses native language questions from local educational materials. All prompts provided in respective native languages, citing that 'providing the prompt in English does not result in performance gains.'

geographic_representation.primary_region: Central Asia and Western Asia (Turkic-speaking regions)
geographic_representation.evidence: Paper states in Limitations: 'some major Turkic languages, such as Turkmen, Kyrgyz [sic — likely an error as Kyrgyz is included] and Bashkir are not included. We are hoping to extend our benchmark with more languages in further editions.' Languages cover a broad geographic span from Turkey to China.
